_source: ColdFusion Short, watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18: frames at 0/0.5/1/2/3/5 s then every 3-5 s to the end, word timings from YouTube's transcript panel (about 175 words a minute). Our own descriptions. 95K views.

hook.firstFrame: a white title box at the top asking if the country's banks are a joke, news footage of a bank branch in a band below, bold caption words
hook.firstLine: Calls the country's banking system a farce.

shots.picture: fixed white title box top; TV news footage of a bank branch in a middle band over a blurred copy of itself
shoppers walking in a mall (stock footage), a news ticker band
white outline map of the country, the south-east fills orange, a dollar sign, four bank logos below
a report's stacked bar chart of bank market share, page drifting
3D glowing bank towers in red and purple light, logos lit on top, rising
3D houses on a street with red 'Price drop' signs and arrows, camera sliding past
stock footage of office workers and a top-down handshake
huge white '70%' on black with a red starburst and a yellow diamond popping beside it
aerial footage of rows of suburban houses
the host talking to camera, a ranking table slides over the lower half then away

lines.gist: the banking system is a farce; four banks pull money away from real business
those four hold about three quarters of the market, by two estimates
that concentration has led to silly results
with no competition they all do one thing: home loans, unlike banks abroad
most of their lending is housing, which bends the whole economy
the country ranks below much poorer nations on an economic-complexity index; host's aside

whyItWorks: A fixed title box at the top states the question for the whole Short; the footage band changes under it.
Captions are big word-by-word capitals with one key word coloured, so it plays on mute.
The payoff is a surprising comparison (ranked below poorer countries), not the first figure.
Clipped from a long video: landscape footage in a centre band, a blurred copy filling the rest.
